cues.text: Here is a simple, disciplined trading plan.
cues.say: Here is a simple, disciplined trading plan.

cues.text: A $100,000 balance. Five trades a day. One percent risk on each.
cues.say: A one hundred thousand dollar balance. Five trades a day. One percent risk on each.

cues.text: Each position risks $1,000. That is your stop loss.
cues.say: Each position risks one thousand dollars. That is your stop loss.

cues.text: The target is 3 to 5 percent: $3,000 to $5,000 per trade.
cues.say: The target is three to five percent. Three to five thousand dollars per trade.

cues.text: And once a trade is in profit, the stop loss moves to break-even.
cues.say: And once a trade is in profit, the stop loss moves to break-even.

cues.text: An example day. Two trades hit take profit: plus $3,000 each.
cues.say: An example day. Two trades hit take profit. Plus three thousand each.

cues.text: One reaches the profit zone, then returns to break-even: zero.
cues.say: One reaches the profit zone, then returns to break-even. Zero.

cues.text: One hits the stop loss: minus $1,000.
cues.say: One hits the stop loss. Minus one thousand.

cues.text: And one closes at 5 percent: plus $5,000.
cues.say: And one closes at five percent. Plus five thousand.

cues.text: The day: plus $10,000. Ten percent.
cues.say: The day: plus ten thousand dollars. Ten percent.

cues.text: The edge is the risk-to-reward, not the win rate.
cues.say: The edge is the risk-to-reward, not the win rate.

cues.text: At one to three, you break even winning just one trade in four.
cues.say: At one to three, you break even winning just one trade in four.

cues.text: Even a bad day, one win and four losses, costs only $1,000.
cues.say: Even a bad day, one win and four losses, costs only one thousand dollars.
